newsitem.title: USA: Wake County, N.C., approves arena financing plan.
newsitem.headline: Wake County, N.C., approves arena financing plan.

text.p: North Carolina's Wake County Commission has approved a financing agreement allocating an additional $48 million of hotel bed tax revenues for a basketball arena.
Commissioners unanimously approved the plan Monday, making final the deal previously agreed to by the City of Raleigh.

The approval will allow the Centennial Authority to begin bidding on construction of the $120 million arena. The 21,000-seat facility will be home to the North Carolina State University basketball team and is scheduled to open in mid-1999.
The Centennial Authority already had $72 million for the project, including $22 million previously earmarked from the hotel tax plus state funds and money raised by university boosters.

The deal gives the authority an additional $48 million in bed tax revenues, and the option to repay the debt over 10 years. It also requires the tax-exempt facility to pay $1.5 million annually in lieu of property taxes.
Authority executive director Sims Hinds said the authority would use a bank loan to start construction and finance the rest with tax-exempt bonds.
"Some time before the year's over we will do a bond issue. We need to do enough to end up with $48 million of net construction funds," he said.
That would put the size of the issue at $55 million to $57 million, depending on market conditions.
